learn.title: API integration, caching, configuration and automated deployment
objectives: Choose an Azure API Management tier (Consumption, Developer, Basic, Standard, Premium and the v2 tiers) and design products, subscriptions, policies, versions, revisions and self-hosted gateways
Recommend a caching layer: Azure Managed Redis (or Azure Cache for Redis) for cache-aside and session state, Azure Front Door for edge caching, and API Management response caching
Design application configuration with Azure App Configuration: labels, feature flags, snapshots, geo-replication and Key Vault references
Recommend infrastructure as code and pipelines: Bicep, ARM, Terraform, template specs, deployment stacks, GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines
Design low-risk releases with deployment slots, blue-green and canary patterns, and self-service environments with Azure Deployment Environments
concepts: API Management products and subscriptions
A product groups one or more APIs for a set of consumers. Products can require a subscription key and administrator approval, and policies such as rate limits can be applied at product scope.
Versions vs revisions

A version is a separate, consumer-visible API (selected by path, header or query string) used for breaking changes. A revision is a non-breaking change to one version that you can test and then make current.
Self-hosted gateway

A containerised API Management gateway that runs on-premises or in other clouds, close to the APIs, while configuration is managed from Azure. It's available in the Developer and Premium (classic) tiers.
Rate limit vs quota
rate-limit and rate-limit-by-key cap calls in a short renewal period to protect backends from bursts. quota and quota-by-key cap total calls or bandwidth over a longer period, for example per month.
Cache-aside pattern

The application reads from the cache first; on a miss it loads data from the data store and writes it to the cache. Updates write to the store and invalidate the cached item, and a TTL limits staleness.
Azure Managed Redis tiers

Memory Optimized (high memory-to-vCPU, lower throughput), Balanced, Compute Optimized (highest throughput) and Flash Optimized (moves cold data to NVMe for very large, cost-effective caches). Flash Optimized doesn't support active geo-replication or RediSearch.
API Management response caching
cache-lookup and cache-store policies cache whole responses in the built-in cache or an external Redis-compatible cache. The Consumption tier has no built-in cache, so it needs an external cache.
App Configuration labels and snapshots
Labels give one key several values, for example per environment or version. A snapshot is an immutable, named set of key-values that an app can load for a repeatable release or a quick rollback.
Key Vault references in App Configuration

App Configuration stores only the secret's URI. The application's configuration provider resolves the secret from Key Vault using the application's own identity, so that identity needs read access to the secret.
Feature flags and filters

Feature flags turn functionality on or off without redeploying. Filters such as targeting (users, groups, percentage) and time window control who gets the feature and when; variant flags support A/B tests.
Template specs and deployment stacks

A template spec stores a versioned ARM or Bicep template as an Azure resource shared through Azure RBAC. A deployment stack manages a set of resources as one unit, can delete or detach resources removed from the template, and can deny changes made outside the stack. Together they replace Azure Blueprints.
Deployment slots

Live App Service apps with their own host names (Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers). A swap warms up the source slot before switching routing, settings marked as slot settings stay in place, and a percentage of production traffic can be routed to a slot for canary testing.
comparisons: Consumption vs v2 vs classic Premium

Consumption is serverless, billed per call, with no developer portal or built-in cache. Basic v2 and Standard v2 offer fast provisioning, and Standard v2 can reach private backends through VNet integration. Premium v2 adds VNet injection and availability zones. Premium (classic) is the only tier with multi-region deployment and supports the self-hosted gateway.
Azure Managed Redis vs Front Door vs API Management cache

Azure Managed Redis is a shared in-memory data store for application data, session state and semantic caching. Front Door caches static and cacheable HTTP content at edge locations close to users. API Management caching stores whole API responses at the gateway to offload backends.
App Configuration vs Key Vault vs App Service app settings

App Configuration holds shared, labelled settings and feature flags for many apps. Key Vault holds secrets, keys and certificates. App Service app settings are per-app environment variables that can reference either service.
Bicep vs ARM JSON vs Terraform

Bicep is Azure's concise declarative language that compiles to ARM JSON and needs no state file. ARM JSON is the underlying format. Terraform works across clouds and providers but needs a managed state file, usually in Azure Storage with locking.

Both run YAML pipelines and support workload identity federation to Azure. GitHub Actions uses environments with protection rules; Azure Pipelines uses environments with approvals and checks, variable groups and service connections.

Blue-green deploys a full parallel environment and switches all traffic at once, with fast rollback by switching back. Canary sends a small share of traffic to the new version first and increases it as health signals stay good.
traps: Choosing Consumption when the design needs a developer portal, a built-in cache, VNet access or request logs in Log Analytics.
Assuming Premium v2 or Standard v2 supports multi-region deployment or the self-hosted gateway; only Premium (classic) offers multi-region, and the self-hosted gateway needs Developer or Premium.
Expecting App Configuration to read Key Vault secrets for the app; the app's own identity must have access to the secret.
Using labels to separate environments that need different access permissions; App Configuration access control is per store, so use separate stores.
Forgetting that managed identities and slot-specific settings don't move during a slot swap, and that auto swap isn't supported for Linux web apps or Web App for Containers.
Picking Flash Optimized Azure Managed Redis when the design needs active geo-replication or vector search.
revision: Breaking API change = new version; non-breaking change = new revision, then make it current.
Self-hosted gateway runs near the backend and needs Developer or Premium (classic); Developer has no SLA.
Cache-aside: read cache, load on miss, invalidate on write, set a TTL (add jitter to avoid mass expiry).
Semantic caching in API Management uses Azure Managed Redis with the RediSearch module, which you enable only when you create the cache.
App Configuration: labels for variants, snapshots for immutable releases, sentinel key for refresh, geo-replication for resilience, Key Vault for secrets.
GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines should authenticate with workload identity federation (OIDC), not stored client secrets.
Template specs share versioned templates; deployment stacks manage lifecycle and deny settings; both replace Azure Blueprints.
Deployment slots need Standard or higher; use swap with preview to validate, traffic routing for canary and an immediate swap back to roll back.
